title: Bekhorot 32
description: Why the meat of an animal tithe may be sold for orphans and by inclusion in its bones, how “it shall not be redeemed” comes to mean “it may not be sold” in three different ways, and the dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel over who may eat a blemished firstborn.
topics: 🧒 Orphans’ animal tithe sold in the usual way, and Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak’s verse
🦴 May the meat’s price be included in the bones? A small animal or a large one, this locale or that
🔗 “It shall not be redeemed” and “And it shall not be redeemed”: the verbal analogy to dedications, and which phrase is free
🔁 Passing and passing, geula and pediya, and the word “it” that leaves out the firstborn
📜 Rava: dedications are consecrated with the owner and non-sacred with the priest
🐑 Rav Ashi: alive it makes a substitute and cannot be redeemed, so “redeemed” must mean “sold”
🍽️ Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel: may an Israelite, or even a gentile, eat of a blemished firstborn?

a1.he: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִישּׁוֹם מֵחַיִּים — לָא גְּזוּר רַבָּנַן, וּבְיַתְמֵי אוֹקְמוּהָ רַבָּנַן אַדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא.

a2.he: וְאַף רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים שֶׁמּוֹכְרִים אוֹתוֹ כְּדַרְכּוֹ?

a3.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״רַק בְּכׇל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר״, אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ בְּרָכָה מֵחַיִּים אֶלָּא לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.

a4.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַבְלִיעוֹ בַּעֲצָמוֹת? רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי, חַד אָמַר: מַבְלִיעוֹ, וְחַד אָמַר: אֵין מַבְלִיעוֹ.

a5.he: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי — הָא בְּדַקָּה, הָא בְּגַסָּה.

a6.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּגַסָּה, וְלָא פְּלִיגִי — מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ, וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ.

a7.he: גּוּפָא: בִּבְכוֹר הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא יִפְדֶּה״, וְנִמְכָּר; בְּמַעֲשֵׂר נֶאֱמַר: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְאֵינוֹ נִמְכָּר, לֹא חַי וְלֹא שָׁחוּט, וְלֹא תָּם וְלֹא בַּעַל מוּם. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי?

a8.he: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא אָמַר רַב, וְכֵן אָמַר רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בְּמַעֲשֵׂר, וְנֶאֱמַר ״וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בַּחֲרָמִים, מָה לְהַלָּן מְכִירָה עִמּוֹ, אַף כָּאן מְכִירָה עִמּוֹ.

a9.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מַפְנֵי, דְּאִי לָא מַפְנֵי, אִיכָּא לְמִפְרַךְ: מָה לַחֲרָמִים, שֶׁכֵּן חָלִים עַל הַכֹּל!

a10.he: לָאיֵי אַפְנוֹיֵי מַפְנֵי, לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בַּחֲרָמִים, וְיִגְמַר מִמַּעֲשֵׂר: מָה מַעֲשֵׂר קָדוֹשׁ וְאֵינוֹ נִגְאָל, אַף חֲרָמִים קְדוֹשִׁים וְאֵינָם נִגְאָלִין. ״וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי? לְאַפְנוֹיֵי.

a11.he: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁכֵּן קָדוֹשׁ לְפָנָיו וּלְאַחֲרָיו!

a12.he: אֶלָּא, לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בַּחֲרָמִים, וְיִגְמַר מִבְּכוֹר: מָה בְּכוֹר קָדוֹשׁ וְאֵינוֹ נִגְאָל, אַף חֲרָמִים קְדוֹשִׁין וְאֵינָן נִגְאָלִין. ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי? לְאַפְנוֹיֵי.

a13.he: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לִבְכוֹר, שֶׁכֵּן קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם!

a14.he: אֶלָּא לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בְּמַעֲשֵׂר, וְיִגְמַר הַעֲבָרָה הַעֲבָרָה מִבְּכוֹר, מָה בְּכוֹר קָדוֹשׁ וְאֵינוֹ נִגְאָל, אַף מַעֲשֵׂר קָדוֹשׁ וְאֵינוֹ נִגְאָל. ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר לְמָה לִי? לְאַפְנוֹיֵי.

a15.he: וְאַכַּתִּי, בְּמַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי לָא, מַפְנֵי דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ כִּדְפָרְכִינַן!

a17.he: בְּכוֹר נָמֵי נֵילַף ״גְּאוּלָּה״ ״גְּאוּלָּה״ מֵחֲרָמִים! דְּמַעֲשֵׂר מַפְנֵי, דִּבְכוֹר לָא מַפְנֵי.

a18.he: וּמַאי חָזֵית דְּלֹא תִפְדֶּה דִּבְכוֹר — לְגוּפֵיהּ, וּדְמַעֲשֵׂר — לְאַפְנוֹיֵי? וְאֵימָא: דְּמַעֲשֵׂר — לְגוּפֵיהּ, דִּבְכוֹר — לְאַפְנוֹיֵי!

a19.he: דָּנִין גְּאוּלָּה מִגְּאוּלָּה, וְאֵין דָּנִין פְּדִיָּיה מִגְּאוּלָּה.

a20.he: מַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? הָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״וְשָׁב הַכֹּהֵן״ ״וּבָא הַכֹּהֵן״ — זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!

a21.he: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ, אֲבָל אִיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ — מִדְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ יָלְפִינַן.

a22.he: וְלֵילַף בְּכוֹר ״הַעֲבָרָה״ ״הַעֲבָרָה״ מִמַּעֲשֵׂר, דְּהָא מַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי גָּמַר ״גְּאוּלָּה״ ״גְּאוּלָּה״ מֵחֲרָמִים!

a23.he: מִיעֵט רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי חֲרָמִים, ״הוּא״ — ״הוּא״ וְלֹא בְּכוֹר. וְאֵימָא ״הוּא״ וְלֹא מַעֲשֵׂר! מַעֲשֵׂר גְּאוּלָּה כְּמוֹתוֹ.

a24.he: רָבָא אָמַר, ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דַּחֲרָמִים לָא צְרִיךְ, דְּאִיתַנְהוּ הֵיכָא? אִי בֵּי בְעָלִים — הֶקְדֵּשׁ נִינְהוּ, אִי בֵּי כֹהֵן — חוּלִּין נִינְהוּ.

a25.he: דְּתַנְיָא: חֲרָמִים, כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהֵן בְּבֵית בְּעָלִים — הֲרֵי הֵן כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״. נְתָנָן לְכֹהֵן — הֲרֵי הֵן כְּחוּלִּין לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ יִהְיֶה״. ״לֹא

b1.he: יִגָּאֵל״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי? אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לַחֲרָמִים — תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְמַעֲשֵׂר. אֵימָא תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לִבְכוֹר? מַעֲשֵׂר גְּאוּלָּה כְּמוֹתוֹ.

b2.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דְּמַעֲשֵׂר — לֹא יִמָּכֵר הוּא. אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל״.

b3.he: אֵימָתַי עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה — מֵחַיִּים, אֵימָתַי אֵינוֹ נִגְאָל — מֵחַיִּים, הָא לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה — נִגְאָל, הָא בָּעֵי הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה!

b4.he: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — לֹא יִמָּכֵר הוּא.

b5.he: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?

b6.he: אֲנַן הָכִי קָאָמְרִינַן: מִי אִיכָּא דְּמֵחַיִּים לָא מִיפְּרִיק, וּלְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה מִיפְּרִיק? אַלְּמָה לָא מֵחַיִּים דְּאַלִּימָא קְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ — לָא מִיפְּרִיק, לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה דְּאַקֵּיל לֵיהּ קְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ — מִיפְּרִיק!

b7.he: וְלָא כֹּל דְּכֵן הוּא? וּמָה מֵחַיִּים דְּאַלִּים לְמִיתְפַּס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ — לָא מִיפְּרִיק, לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה דְּלָא אַלִּים לְמִיתְפָּס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ — מִיפְּרִיק? אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — לֹא יִמָּכֵר הוּא.

b8.he: וְלִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״! אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אִיזְדַּבּוֹנֵי הוּא דְּלָא מִזְדַּבַּן, דְּקָא עָבֵיד עוֹבָדִין דְּחוֹל, אֲבָל אִיפְּרוֹקֵי — מִיפְּרִיק, דְּהָא עָיְילִי דָּמָיו לְהֶקְדֵּשׁ. לְהָכִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, דְּלָא אִיזְדַּבּוֹנֵי מִיזְדַּבַּן וְלָא אִיפְּרוֹקֵי מִיפְּרִיק.

b9.he: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: לֹא יִמָּנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַכֹּהֵן לַבְּכוֹר, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין, וַאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי.

b10.he: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: בְּכוֹר אֵין נִמְנִין עָלָיו אֶלָּא חֲבוּרָה שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ כֹּהֲנִים, דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֲפִילּוּ זָרִים. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַתִּיר אֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי.

b11.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי? דִּכְתִיב ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָךְ וְגוֹ׳״, מָה הָתָם כֹּהֲנִים — אִין, יִשְׂרָאֵל — לָא, אַף הָכָא כֹּהֲנִים — אִין, יִשְׂרָאֵל — לָא.

messages.text: Continued from 31b: Rava derived from “it shall not be redeemed” that by Torah law an animal tithe may be sold after its slaughter, and said the Sages decreed against selling it after slaughter only for an item appraised when the animal is alive, that is, its meat.

But with regard to an item that is not appraised when an animal is sold when alive, e.g., the hide and sinews, as these are not primary contributing factors to the animal’s value, the Sages did not decree that one may not sell such items after the animal’s slaughter. Consequently, the meat of an animal tithe offering may be sold by means of inclusion in the animal’s hide, fat, sinews, and horns.

notes.he: כגון העור והגידין שחשיבות שום דמי הבהמה אינו בשביל העור הלכך בהבלעה שרי אפי' דגדול וביתמי משום השבת אבידה אוקמוה אדאורייתא דלאחר שחיטה מוכרו כדרכו:
notes.en: And an item that is not appraised when alive: such as the hide and the sinews, since the importance of the appraisal of the animal’s value is not on account of the hide. Therefore, by means of inclusion it is permitted, even [the animal tithe] of an adult. And for orphans, because of [the principle of] returning a lost item, they kept it at Torah law, that after slaughter one sells it in its usual manner.

notes.he: היינו עור דאינו נישום אלא לאחר מיתה לא גזרו רבנן לאחר שחיטה דאינו נמכר בהבלעה אטו קודם שחיטה אלא נמכר בהבלעה:
notes.en: An item that is not appraised when alive: that is, the hide, which is appraised only after death. The Rabbis did not decree after slaughter that it may not be sold by inclusion on account of before slaughter; rather, it is sold by inclusion.

messages.text: And with regard to a case of young orphans, the Sages established the halakha as if by Torah law, and therefore the meat may be sold in its usual manner.

notes.he: וביתמי אוקמוה רבנן אדאוריי' דלא גזרו בהו משום תקנת יתומים אלא אוקמוה אדאורייתא דמחיים אינו נמכר הא לאחר שחיטה נמכר אפילו שלא בהבלעה:
notes.en: And with orphans the Rabbis kept it at Torah law: they did not decree about them, for the benefit of the orphans, but kept it at Torah law, that while alive it is not sold, but after slaughter it is sold even not by inclusion.

messages.text: And even Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak holds in accordance with that opinion of Rava, that by Torah law, the meat of a blemished animal-tithe offering may be sold in the normal manner.

notes.he: דמעשר לאחר שחיטה דאורייתא שרי למכור:
notes.en: He holds in accordance with that of Rava: that an animal tithe after slaughter is permitted to be sold by Torah law.

notes.dh: ואף רב שמואל בר רב יצחק סבר לה להא דרבא
notes.he: פי' מקרא אחרינא ולא מטעמיה:
notes.en: And even Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak holds in accordance with that of Rava: that is, from another verse, and not for his reason.

messages.text: From where is it derived that one may sell the meat of a blemished animal-tithe offering of young orphans in its usual manner, without having to resort to the method of inclusion?

It is derived from a verse, as it is stated in a verse discussing consecrated animals that became blemished: “Notwithstanding, after all the desire of your soul, you may slaughter and eat flesh, according to the blessing of the Lord your God”.

verse.he: רַק בְּכׇל־אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח ׀ וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר כְּבִרְכַּת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן־לְךָ בְּכׇל־שְׁעָרֶיךָ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יֹאכְלֶנּוּ כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃
verse.en: But whenever you desire, you may slaughter and eat meat in any of your settlements, according to the blessing that the ETERNAL your God has granted you. The impure and the pure alike may partake of it, as of the gazelle and the deer.

notes.he: מוקמינן בספרי דבפסולי המוקדשין מישתעי וכתיב תזבח ואכלת:
notes.en: Notwithstanding, after all the desire of your soul: in the Sifrei we establish that it speaks of disqualified consecrated animals, and it is written “you may slaughter and eat.”

messages.text: Now which is the item that has no blessing when it is alive, i.e., it is prohibited to derive benefit from it, but it does have a blessing after its slaughter, as indicated by the verse “You may slaughter…according to the blessing of the Lord your God”? You must say that this is the meat of the animal tithe offering.

notes.dh: איזהו דבר שאין בו ברכה מחיים
notes.he: שאין נהנין מהם מחיים דהא שאר קדשים אם נפל בהן מום פודן ויכול למוכרן מחיים לכל מי שירצה:
notes.en: Which is the item that has no blessing when alive: that one may not derive benefit from them while alive; for other consecrated animals, if a blemish befell them, one redeems them and may sell them while alive to whomever he wishes.

notes.he: דכתיב ביה לא יגאל דאינו נמכר מחיים וכתב דלאחר זביחה איכא ברכה וההוא ברכה מכירה היא דדומיא דברכה שאסר לך מחיים התיר לך לאחר שחיטה ומה ברכה היתה ראויה בו מחיים מכירה. אלמא לאחר שחיטה נמכר מדאורייתא והא דתני אינו נמכר שחוט דרבנן הוא הילכך ביתמי מוקמינן אדאורייתא:
notes.en: Rather, this is the animal tithe: of which it is written “it shall not be redeemed,” that it is not sold while alive; and it is written that after slaughter there is a blessing. And that blessing is selling, for, parallel to the blessing that He prohibited to you while alive, He permitted to you after slaughter; and what blessing would have been fitting for it while alive? Selling. Evidently, after slaughter it is sold by Torah law, and that which is taught, “it is not sold slaughtered,” is rabbinic. Therefore, for orphans we keep it at Torah law.

notes.dh: איזהו דבר שאין בו ברכה מחיים
notes.he: כלומר דמחיים אסור למוכרו וליהנות ממנו אלא לאחר שחיטה מותר הוי אומר מעשר בהמה של יתומים דאי דגדול רבנן גזרי ביה לאחר שחיטה אטו לפני שחיטה. ואי שאר פסולי המוקדשין אפי' מחיים נמכרין לאחר פדיונן:
notes.en: Which is the item that has no blessing when alive: that is, while alive it is prohibited to sell it and to derive benefit from it, but after slaughter it is permitted. You must say: the animal tithe of orphans. For if of an adult, the Rabbis decreed about it after slaughter on account of before slaughter. And if other disqualified consecrated animals, even while alive they are sold after their redemption. [The printed edition adds a note: It appears from Rabbeinu’s wording that he read in the Gemara “this is the animal tithe of orphans.” This is not understood, since for adults too it is permitted by Torah law to sell after slaughter, and this Amora is speaking of the verse; this requires further study.]

messages.text: § The baraita cited earlier teaches that the Sages permitted the inclusion of the value of a blemished animal-tithe offering’s meat in the cost of its hide, fat, sinews, and horns. In this regard, a dilemma was raised before the Sages: What is the halakha with regard to including the value of the meat in the cost of the animal’s bones?

notes.he: דמי בשר מעשר בהמה של גדול עם דמי העצמות:
notes.en: What is it to include: the value of the meat of the animal tithe of an adult together with the value of the bones.

notes.he: הבשר בדמי העצמות:
notes.en: In its bones: [to include] the meat in the value of the bones.

messages.text: Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, disputed this matter. One says that one may include the value in the cost of the bones, and one says one may not include it.

And they do not disagree. This one, who maintains that one may not include the value in the cost of the bones, is referring to a small, domesticated animal, whose bones are incapable of being fashioned into utensils and are therefore never sold. That one, who holds that one may include the value in the cost of the bones, is referring to a large, domesticated animal, whose bones can be used and are therefore sold.
messages.quote: One says that one may include the value in the cost of the bones, and one says one may not include it

notes.he: אין העצמות ראויים לכלום ואין מבליעין:
notes.en: A small animal: the bones are not fit for anything, and one does not include.

notes.he: ראויין העצמות לקתתא דנגרי וחציני ומבליעין:
notes.en: A large animal: the bones are fit for handles of carpenters’ tools and of axes, and one includes.

notes.he: עצמותיה חשובין למלאכה ויכול להבליעו בהן:
notes.en: This is with a large animal: its bones are valuable for craftwork, and one may include [the meat] in them.

messages.text: And if you wish, say instead that both this one and that one are referring even to a large, domesticated animal, and still they do not disagree. This Sage rules in accordance with the custom of his locale, and that Sage rules in accordance with the custom of his locale. In other words, in certain places the custom is to use the bones and sell them, while elsewhere they do not.

notes.he: עושין כלים מעצמות ובאתריה דמר אין עושין כלים מעצמות ואין מבליעין:
notes.en: In the locale of this Sage: they make utensils from bones; and in the locale of that Sage they do not make utensils from bones, and one does not include.

notes.he: מאן דאמר מבליעו באתריה חשיבי עצמות דעבדי מינייהו חלילין. ובאתריה דמר דאמר אין מבליעו לא עבדי מיניה חלילין:
notes.en: Each Sage according to his locale: the one who says one includes [lived where] bones are valued, for they make flutes from them; and in the locale of the Sage who says one does not include, they do not make flutes from them.

messages.text: § The Gemara returns to the matter itself, stated in the baraita:

With regard to a firstborn male animal offering the verse states: “You shall not redeem” (Numbers 18:17), but it may be sold while alive, by the priest to whom it belongs. By contrast, with regard to the animal tithe offering, it is stated: “It shall not be redeemed” (Leviticus 27:33), indicating that its sanctity can never be removed from it, and it cannot be sold, not when alive and not when slaughtered, not when unblemished and not when blemished.
From where is this matter derived, that the phrase “it shall not be redeemed” is referring to the prohibition against selling the animal tithe offering?

notes.he: דמעשר אינו נמכר דמאי משמע מכירה מלא יגאל:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: that an animal tithe is not sold; for how does “it shall not be redeemed” imply selling?

messages.alt: and similarly, Rav Dimi says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says
messages.text: It is stated: “It shall not be redeemed,” with regard to the animal tithe offering, and it is stated: “And it shall not be redeemed,” with regard to dedications [baḥaramim], i.e., property that one consecrated by means of the expression: Ḥerem. With regard to dedications, the verse states: “Notwithstanding, any dedicated item…may neither be sold nor redeemed”.

verse.he: אַךְ־כׇּל־חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יַחֲרִם אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה מִכׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ מֵאָדָם וּבְהֵמָה וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ לֹא יִמָּכֵר וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל כׇּל־חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ־קׇדָשִׁים הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But of all that anyone owns, be it human or animal or land-holding, nothing that has been proscribed for GOD may be sold or redeemed; every proscribed thing is totally consecrated to GOD.

notes.he: כתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ח) לא ימכר ולא יגאל כל חרם קדשים וגו':
notes.en: With regard to dedications: it is written (Leviticus 27:28): “It may neither be sold nor redeemed; every dedicated item is most holy,” etc.

messages.text: This is a verbal analogy: Just as there, with regard to dedications, the prohibition against selling is mentioned together with the prohibition against redeeming, so too here, with regard to the animal tithe offering, the prohibition against selling is mentioned together with the prohibition against redeeming.

@Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua It must be that at least one of the phrases “It shall not be redeemed” is free, i.e., at least one of these terms is superfluous in its context, which means that it is included for the specific purpose of the verbal analogy. In such a case the verbal analogy cannot be refuted by logic, whereas if neither phrase is free one can refute the analogy if there is a significant difference between the two cases.

notes.he: שצריך שיהו תיבות הללו לא יגאל מופנין לדרשא זו:
notes.en: Free: for these words “it shall not be redeemed” must be free for this exposition.

messages.text: As, if these terms are not free, the verbal analogy can be refuted: What is notable about dedications, in contrast to the animal tithe offering? They are notable in that they apply to all items one wishes to dedicate, whereas an animal tithe offering applies only to kosher animals.

notes.he: שאם החרים את הקדשים חל חרם עליהן ונותן לכהן כפי טובת הנאה שיש לו בהן כדאמר בערכין בפ' המקדיש שדהו (ערכין דף כח:) תאמר במעשר שאינו חל אלא על החולין ועוד חרם חל על כל העדר ומעשר אינו אלא עשירי:
notes.en: In that they apply to all: for if one declared consecrated items to be dedications, the dedication takes effect on them, and he gives the priest according to the benefit of discretion that he has in them, as it says in Arakhin, in the chapter HaMakdish Sadehu (Arakhin 28b). Would you say the same of the tithe, which takes effect only on non-sacred animals? And furthermore, a dedication takes effect on the entire herd, while the tithe is only the tenth.

notes.he: בין על קדשי קדשים בין על קדשים קלים בין על חולין. מעשר בהמה אינו חל אלא על חולין:
notes.en: In that they apply to all: whether to offerings of the most sacred order, to offerings of lesser sanctity, or to non-sacred property. The animal tithe takes effect only on non-sacred animals.

messages.text: This is not so [la’ai], as at least one of the phrases: “It shall not be redeemed,” is certainly free. How so? Let the verse not state: “It shall not be redeemed,” with regard to dedications, and instead one could derive the prohibition from an animal tithe offering: Just as an animal tithe offering is sacred and may not be redeemed, so too, dedications are also sacred and may not be redeemed.

notes.dh: דלא יאמר לא יגאל בחרמים וגמר ממעשר מה מעשר קדוש ואינו נגאל
notes.he: וא"ת דילמא הוה ילפינן מהקדש דתפדה וי"ל דלחומרא ילפינן א"נ משום דבחרמים כתיב לא ימכר ומוקמינן בהו לא יגאל:
notes.en: Let the verse not state “it shall not be redeemed” with regard to dedications, and derive it from the tithe: just as the tithe is sacred and not redeemed. And if you say: perhaps we would derive it from [ordinary] consecrated property, which is redeemed? One can say that we derive toward stringency. Alternatively, because with regard to dedications it is written “it may not be sold,” we would apply “it shall not be redeemed” to them as well.

notes.he: דכתיב כל חרם קדש קדשים הוא:
notes.en: So too dedications are sacred: as it is written, “Every dedicated item is most holy.”

messages.text: Why then do I need the phrase “It shall not be redeemed” that the Merciful One writes, in the case of dedications? It is evidently to be considered free to enable the verbal analogy.

notes.he: לאפנויי ולמילף למעשר מה לא יגאל דחרמים לא ימכר נמי אף לא יגאל דמעשר לא ימכר נמי:
notes.en: To be free, and to derive the tithe from it: just as “it shall not be redeemed” of dedications [comes with] “it shall not be sold” too, so too “it shall not be redeemed” of the tithe [means] “it shall not be sold” too.

messages.text: It is still possible that the phrase “It shall not be redeemed,” written with regard to dedications, is not free, as the suggested derivation stated above can be refuted: What is notable about the animal tithe offering? It is notable in that there is sanctity before it and after it.
messages.quote: It is evidently to be considered free

notes.he: דאיצטריך לא יגאל דחרמים דממעשר לא גמירי דמה למעשר שכן קדש לפניו ולאחריו שאם קרא לעשירי תשיעי ולתשיעי עשירי ולאחד עשר עשירי שלשתן מקודשים:
notes.en: It can be refuted: so that “it shall not be redeemed” of dedications is needed, since we cannot learn it from the tithe: what is notable about the tithe, that it is sacred before it and after it? For if he called the tenth “ninth,” and the ninth “tenth,” and the eleventh “tenth,” all three are consecrated.

notes.he: כדתנן קרא לתשיעי עשירי ולעשירי עשירי ולאחד עשר עשירי שלשתן מקודשין. מה שאין כן בחרמים:
notes.en: In that it sanctifies before it and after it: as we learned: if he called the ninth “tenth,” and the tenth “tenth,” and the eleventh “tenth,” all three are consecrated. This is not so with dedications.

messages.text: If, instead of proclaiming as the tithe the tenth animal that one counted, one inadvertently proclaimed either the ninth animal or the eleventh animal as the tithe, the mistakenly proclaimed animal assumes the sacred status of the animal tithe offering. By contrast, one cannot inadvertently dedicate property to the Temple. Since the case of the animal tithe offering includes a stringency not shared by dedications, the phrase “It shall not be redeemed” is required to teach that dedications may not be redeemed, and is therefore not free for the verbal analogy.

Rather, let the verse not state: “It shall not be redeemed,” with regard to dedications, and instead one can derive the prohibition from the firstborn offering: Just as the firstborn offering is sacred and may not be redeemed, as the verse states: “You shall not redeem it” (Numbers 18:17), so too, dedications are also sacred and may not be redeemed.
Why do I need the phrase “It shall not be redeemed” that the Merciful One writes in the case of dedications? It is evidently to be considered free to enable the verbal analogy to the animal tithe.

It is possible that the phrase “It shall not be redeemed” is not free, as the above derivation can be refuted: What is notable about the firstborn offering? It is notable in that its sanctity is from the womb, whereas dedications require an act of consecration.
messages.quote: It is evidently to be considered free

notes.he: במעשר כדפרכינן גבי חרמים מה לבכור שכן קדושתו מרחם תאמר במעשר שאין קדושתו מרחם ולהכי איצטריך לא יגאל דמעשר:
notes.en: For it can be refuted: with regard to the tithe, as we refuted regarding dedications: what is notable about the firstborn, that its sanctity is from the womb? Would you say the same of the tithe, whose sanctity is not from the womb? And that is why “it shall not be redeemed” of the tithe is needed.

messages.text: Rather, let the verse not say: “It shall not be redeemed,” with regard to the animal tithe offering, and instead one can derive the prohibition from a verbal analogy from the term of passing stated there and the term of passing stated in the case of a firstborn. With regard to an animal tithe offering the verse states: “Whatsoever passes under the rod” (Leviticus 27:32), and in the case of the firstborn offering it is stated: “And you shall cause to pass all that opens the womb, to the Lord” (Exodus 13:12).

Just as the firstborn offering is sacred and may not be redeemed, so too, an animal tithe offering is also sacred and may not be redeemed. Why do I need the phrase “It shall not be redeemed” that the Merciful One writes with regard to animal tithe offerings? It is evidently to be considered free to enable the verbal analogy to dedications.

But still, the phrase “It shall not be redeemed,” written with regard to the animal tithe offering, is itself not free, as the analogy between the animal tithe offering and the firstborn offering can be refuted as we refuted the analogy between the firstborn offering and dedications, since the firstborn offering is notable in that it is sanctified from the womb.
messages.quote: Just as the firstborn offering is sacred and may not be redeemed

notes.he: איכא למיפרך כדפרכינן מה לבכור שכן קדושתו מרחם:
notes.en: It can be refuted as we refuted: what is notable about the firstborn, that its sanctity is from the womb?

messages.text: The term “And you shall cause to pass,” written in the context of the firstborn, is a superfluous verse, as it could have simply stated: All that opens the womb is to be for the Lord. Consequently, it is free to enable the verbal analogy.

verse.he: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כׇל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר ׀ שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: you shall set apart for GOD every first issue of the womb: every male firstling that your cattle drop shall be GOD’s.

notes.he: ומופנה לגזירה שוה ללמד העברה העברה על מעשר שלא יגאל ואין משיבין עליה הילכך לא יגאל דמעשר מופנה הוא. ומאי טעמא האי קרא יתירא דמצי למכתב כל פטר רחם לה' כדכתיב קרא אחרינא (שמות יג) כל פטר רחם לה' והעברת למה לי ש"מ קרא יתירא הוא:
notes.en: And “you shall cause to pass” is a superfluous verse: and it is free for a verbal analogy, to teach “passing” and “passing” for the tithe, that it shall not be redeemed, and one does not refute it. Therefore “it shall not be redeemed” of the tithe is free. And why is this verse superfluous? Because it could have written “all that opens the womb is the Lord’s,” as another verse writes (Exodus 13), “all that opens the womb is Mine.” Why do I need “and you shall cause to pass”? Conclude from it that it is a superfluous verse.

notes.he: כלומר דלא צריך הכתוב לומר והעברת שהיה יכול לומר ונתת כל פטר רחם. אלא למה נכתב בלשון והעברת להיקישא ואין משיבין על ההיקישא ומייתר ליה לא יגאל במעשר למילף מלא יגאל דחרמים מה להלן מכירה עמו אף כאן מכירה עמו. לעבור דמעשר ליכא למימר יתירא דמעשר ילפינן מבכור:
notes.en: And “you shall cause to pass” is superfluous: that is, the verse did not need to say “and you shall cause to pass,” for it could have said “and you shall give all that opens the womb.” Rather, why was it written in the language of “you shall cause to pass”? For the comparison, and one does not refute a comparison; and that leaves “it shall not be redeemed” free in the tithe, to learn from “it shall not be redeemed” of dedications: just as there selling is with it, so too here selling is with it. One cannot say that the “passing” of the tithe is superfluous, since the tithe is learned from the firstborn.

messages.text: In sum, the Gemara is suggesting that due to the term “And you shall cause to pass,” there is a verbal analogy between the animal tithe offering and the firstborn offering, from which it is derived that the animal tithe offering may not be redeemed. This means that the phrase “It shall not be redeemed,” written with regard to the animal tithe offering, is free to enable the verbal analogy with dedications, from which the prohibition against selling the meat of the animal tithe offering is derived.

messages.caption: How Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan’s verbal analogy brings the prohibition of selling from dedications to the animal tithe, but not to the firstborn.

messages.text: With regard to a firstborn offering as well, let us derive that one may not sell its meat from a verbal analogy between the expression of redemption written there and the expression of redemption written in the context of dedications. This would contradict the ruling of the baraita that a firstborn offering can be sold after it enters the possession of the priest.

notes.dh: בכור נמי נילף גאולה גאולה מחרמים
notes.he: דלא ימכר דאע"ג דלא כתב בבכור גאולה כתב ביה פדייה (שם) והיא היא:
notes.en: Let us derive the firstborn too, redemption and redemption from dedications: that it may not be sold; for although “redemption” [geula] is not written with regard to the firstborn, “redemption” [pediya] is written with regard to it (ibid.), and it is the same thing.

notes.he: מחרמים ולא יהא נמכר דמעשר מופנה כו'. ונילף בכור שלא יהא נמכר העברה העברה ממעשר דהא אשכחן מעשר שאסור במכירה דגמר גאולה גאולה מחרמים וליגמר בכור ממעשר. הוא דכתיב קדש קדשים הוא דכתיב כל חרם קודש קדשים הוא:
notes.en: Let us derive the firstborn too, redemption: from dedications, and let it not be sold. [Answer:] That of the tithe is free, etc. And let us derive the firstborn, that it not be sold, “passing” and “passing” from the tithe, for we have found that the tithe is prohibited to be sold, since it is derived “redemption” and “redemption” from dedications; let the firstborn be derived from the tithe. [Answer:] “It,” as it is written “most holy it is,” as it is written “every dedicated item is most holy it is.”

messages.text: The expression of redemption in the context of the animal tithe offering is free to enable the verbal analogy to dedications, but the expression of redemption in the context of a firstborn offering is not free, as it is required in its own context to teach that the firstborn offering may not be redeemed and as the source for the halakha of the animal tithe offering.

notes.he: כדאמרן הלכך דיינינן ליה גזירה שוה מחרמים אבל פדייה דבכור לא מפני דאיצטריך לגופיה ולאגמורי נמי אמעשר בהעברה העברה:
notes.en: Redemption of the tithe is free: as we said; therefore we judge it by a verbal analogy from dedications. But the pediya of the firstborn is not free, since it is needed for itself and also to teach the tithe through “passing” and “passing.”

messages.text: And what did you see that you said that the phrase “you shall not redeem” written in the context of a firstborn offering is not free, but is necessary for itself, i.e., to teach that it may not be redeemed, and yet the expression of redemption written with regard to the animal tithe offering is free to enable the verbal analogy, as the halakha of its redemption is derived from the firstborn? But one can say the reverse, that the expression of redemption written in the context of the animal tithe offering is for itself, whereas that written with regard to a firstborn offering is free.

notes.he: דפדייה דבכור לגופיה ולאגמורי אמעשר ולא יגאל דמעשר לאפנויי ולמיגמר גזירה שוה מחרמים אימא לא יגאל דמעשר לגופיה דלא יפדה ולאגמורי אבכור בהעברה העברה ודבכור לאפנויי ולמיגמר גזירה שוה מחרמים דאסור במכירה:
notes.en: And what did you see: that the pediya of the firstborn is for itself and to teach the tithe, and “it shall not be redeemed” of the tithe is to be free and to derive a verbal analogy from dedications? Say instead that “it shall not be redeemed” of the tithe is for itself, that it is not redeemed, and to teach the firstborn through “passing” and “passing,” and that of the firstborn is to be free and to derive a verbal analogy from dedications, that it is prohibited to be sold.

messages.text: We derive the expression of redemption [geula] written in the context of the animal tithe offering from the expression of redemption [geula] written in the context of dedications, but we do not derive the expression of redemption [pediya] written in the context of a firstborn offering from the different expression of redemption [geula] written in the context of the dedications.
What difference is there whether or not an identical expression is used for a verbal analogy? Didn’t the school of Rabbi Yishmael teach a verbal analogy with regard to leprosy of houses?
messages.quote: but we do not derive the expression of redemption [pediya] … from the different expression of redemption [geula]

messages.text: The verse states: “And the priest shall return [veshav] on the seventh day” (Leviticus 14:39), and another verse with regard to the priest’s visit seven days later states: “And the priest shall come [uva] and look” (Leviticus 14:44). This returning and this coming have the same meaning and one can therefore derive by verbal analogy that the same halakha that applies if the leprosy had spread at the conclusion of the first week also applies if it had spread again by the end of the following week.

verse.he: וְשָׁב הַכֹּהֵן בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וְרָאָה וְהִנֵּה פָּשָׂה הַנֶּגַע בְּקִירֹת הַבָּיִת׃
verse.en: On the seventh day the priest shall return. If he sees that the plague has spread on the walls of the house,

messages.text: Here too, the different terms of pediya and geula should not prevent the application of a verbal analogy.

This statement, that the phrases used for a verbal analogy do not have to be identical, applies only where there are no terms that are equivalent to it. But where there are terms that are equivalent to it, we derive the verbal analogy from the terms that are equivalent to it, rather than from the terms that are not equivalent.

But let one derive that it is prohibited to sell the meat of a blemished firstborn offering from the verbal analogy between the expression of passing and the expression of passing, from the case of the animal tithe offering. This should be possible, as the sale of the meat of a blemished animal-tithe offering is also prohibited, as derived by a verbal analogy between the expression of redemption written in its context and the expression of redemption written with regard to dedications, as explained earlier.

notes.he: שיהא אסור במכירה דהא מעשר כבר קים לן דגמרנא ליה גאולה מחרמים:
notes.en: And let us derive the firstborn, passing, from the tithe: that it be prohibited to be sold, for regarding the tithe we have already established that we derive it, redemption [and redemption], from dedications.

messages.text: The Merciful One limits the extension of the prohibition against selling with regard to dedications by adding the term “it” in the verse: “It is most holy to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28). The term “it” teaches that the prohibition against selling applies only to it, i.e., dedications, but not to a firstborn offering.
messages.quote: But let one derive that it is prohibited to sell the meat of a blemished firstborn offering

notes.he: רבא נמי דמשני בסמוך שלא ימכר בחרמים לא צריך אית ליה נמי הוא ולא בכור כדמוכח בפ"ק דתמורה (דף ה:) גבי אי עביד לא מהני דאי לאו הוא הוה ילפינן בכור העברה העברה ממעשר ואביי נמי דמוקי בפ"ק דתמורה הוא בהוייתו יהא מ"מ הוה דריש הוא ולא בכור מדסמך ליה הוא לקדש קדשים דמשמע הוא בקדושתו יהא:
notes.en: “It,” and not the firstborn: Rava too, who answers below that “it shall not be sold” with regard to dedications is not needed, also holds “it, and not the firstborn,” as is evident in the first chapter of Temura (5b), regarding “if one does it, it is not effective”; for were it not for “it,” we would derive the firstborn, “passing” and “passing,” from the tithe. And Abaye too, who establishes “it” in the first chapter of Temura as “it shall remain in its being,” nevertheless would expound “it, and not the firstborn,” since “it” is juxtaposed to “most holy,” which implies: it shall remain in its sanctity.

messages.text: But one can say instead that the term “it” teaches that the prohibition against selling applies to dedications, but not to the animal tithe offering.
messages.quote: but not to a firstborn offering

messages.text: The prohibition against selling applies to the animal tithe offering, with regard to which the expression of redemption is written, just like dedications, while the term “it” limits the prohibition to the firstborn offering.

notes.he: הוה ליה לרבויי בדין חרמים דגאולה כתב ביה כמו בחרמים ולמעוטי בכור דפדייה כתב ביה:
notes.en: It stands to reason, the tithe: should be included in the law of dedications, since “redemption” [geula] is written with regard to it as with dedications; and the firstborn should be excluded, since pediya is written with regard to it.

messages.text: § There is an alternative explanation for the prohibition against selling the animal tithe. The phrase “It may not be redeemed,” written with regard to dedications, is unnecessary and is therefore free to enable a verbal analogy with the animal tithe offering.

notes.he: ולא משום דגמר מבכור אלא מסברא נפקא לן דאינו בפדייה:
notes.en: “It shall not be redeemed” of dedications is not needed: and not because it is derived from the firstborn, but rather we know by reasoning that it is not subject to redemption.

notes.dh: רבא אמר לא יגאל דחרמים לא צריך
notes.he: כך כתוב בספרים ורש"י גרס לא ימכר משום דדייק דאיתנהו היכא אי בי בעלים הקדש נינהו ואי בלא יגאל קאמר והא קדשי בדק הבית נגאלין ור"ת מפ' דהקדש נינהו קאמר היינו אפי' נפדו דקדש קדשים משמע ליה קדושת הגוף עד בואו ליד כהן ומיהו קשיא לר' דבפ"ק דתמורה (דף ה:) משמע דמוכחינן דאין מועיל פדיון מהוא בהוייתו יהא לאביי דאי עביד מהני ולרבא דאמר לא מהני נפיק מלא יגאל גופיה וא"כ היכי הוה דייק הכא דלא יגאל לא צריך משום דאי בי בעלים הקדש נינהו אפילו נפדו הוא גופה מלא יגאל נפקא ליה לרבא ועוד קשיא אחרת שהקשה רש"י הא דקאמר אם אינו ענין לחרמים תנהו ענין למעשר מאי צריך מעשר ללא יגאל דחרמים הא בגופה כתב ואי משום לא ימכר בקנייה הכי ה"ל למימר ואם אינו ענין לגאולה דבגופה כתב תנהו ענין למכירה א"נ יאמר לא יגאל דחרמים למה לי ש"מ לאפנויי:
notes.en: Rava says: “It shall not be redeemed” of dedications is not needed: so it is written in the books, but Rashi reads “it shall not be sold,” because he infers [from the Gemara’s words] “where are they? If with the owner, they are consecrated”; and if it were speaking of “it shall not be redeemed,” surely items consecrated for Temple maintenance are redeemed! And Rabbeinu Tam explains that “they are consecrated” means even if they were redeemed, for “most holy” implies to him intrinsic sanctity until it comes into the priest’s hand. However, it is difficult for the Ri [our teacher]: in the first chapter of Temura (5b) it is implied that we prove that redemption is not effective from “it shall remain in its being,” according to Abaye, who says that if one does it, it is effective; and according to Rava, who says it is not effective, it is derived from “it shall not be redeemed” itself. If so, how could he infer here that “it shall not be redeemed” is not needed because with the owner they are consecrated even if they were redeemed? Rava derives that very thing from “it shall not be redeemed”! And there is another difficulty, which Rashi raised: what he says, “If it is not relevant to dedications, apply it to the tithe” — why does the tithe need the “it shall not be redeemed” of dedications, when it is written of the tithe itself? And if it is because of “it shall not be sold,” in the sense of acquisition, he should have said this: “If it is not relevant to redemption, which is written of it itself, apply it to selling.” Alternatively, he should have said: “Why do I need ‘it shall not be redeemed’ of dedications? Conclude from it that it is to be free.”

notes.dh: לא יגאל דחרמים לא צריך ולא צריכת למילף מג"ש
notes.he: דאיתנהו היכא החרמים אי בבעלים הקדש נינהו ואסור לפדות קדשים תמימים:
notes.en: “It shall not be redeemed” of dedications is not needed: and you do not need to derive it from a verbal analogy. For where are the dedications? If with the owner, they are consecrated, and it is prohibited to redeem unblemished consecrated animals.

messages.text: As where are the items of dedication, designated for the priests, located? If they are in the owner’s possession, they are considered consecrated and may not be redeemed. And if they are in the priest’s possession, they are considered non-sacred and the priest may sell them.

notes.he: ואינו בפדייה ולא דמי לקדשי מזבח:
notes.en: They are consecrated: and are not subject to redemption, and they are not like offerings consecrated for the altar.

notes.he: ויכול למוכרן כהן לכל מי שירצה:
notes.en: They are non-sacred: and the priest may sell them to whomever he wishes.

messages.text: Dedications, as long as they are in the owner’s possession, are like consecrated property in all respects, as it is stated: “Every dedicated item is most holy to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28). Once the owner gave them to the priest, they are like non-sacred property in all respects, as it is stated: “Every dedicated item in Israel shall be for You” (Numbers 18:14).
messages.lead: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

verse.en: Everything that has been proscribed in Israel shall be yours.

notes.he: הוא אסור במכירה:
notes.en: Every dedicated item is most holy, it: it is prohibited to be sold.

notes.he: ברשות כהן הן כשאר ממונו:
notes.en: Shall be yours: they are in the priest’s domain, like the rest of his property.

notes.he: ונמכרין כדרכן:
notes.en: If he gave them to the priest, they are like non-sacred property: and they are sold in the usual manner.

messages.text: Accordingly, concerning the phrase “It may not …

… be redeemed” that the Merciful One writes, why do I need it? If it is not referring to the matter of dedications, as can be inferred from the baraita, apply it to the matter of the animal tithe offering, teaching that it may not be sold.

notes.he: למכירה:
notes.en: Apply it to the matter of the tithe: for selling.

notes.he: תנהו ענין למעשר האי לא יגאל יתירא ולמכירה:
notes.en: Apply it to the matter of the tithe: this superfluous “it shall not be redeemed,” and for selling.

messages.text: One can say that instead of applying it to the animal tithe offering, apply it to the matter of a firstborn offering.
messages.quote: apply it to the matter of the animal tithe offering

messages.text: The prohibition against selling extends to the animal tithe offering, concerning which the expression of redemption is written, just like dedications, which is not so concerning the firstborn offering.

notes.he: מסתברא דאמעשר שדינן ליה שכן גאולה כמותו כך שמעתי. ויש לי הרבה להשיב חדא דקאמר אי בבעלים הקדש נינהו והרי הקדש בר פדייה שהרי קדשי בדק הבית נפדין כקדשי מזבח כדכתיב ואם המקדיש יגאל את ביתו ובעל כרחיך איצטריך למכתב בחרמים לא יגאל ועוד דקאמר תנהו ענין למעשר ומה לנו להביא לא יגאל אמעשר הרי כבר נאמר בו לא יגאל ואם למכירה קאמר היה לו עוד לומר אם אינו ענין לגאולה תנהו ענין למכירה אי נמי הוה ליה למימר לא יגאל דחרמים למה לי ש"מ לאפנויי ולדון גזירה שוה דמה כאן מכירה עמו אף מעשר מכירה עמו. הילכך מדומה לי דהכי מיבעי לך למיגרס אמר רבא לא ימכר דחרמים לא צריך והכי פירושה רבא אמר בלא גזירה שוה נפקא לן במעשר דאינו נמכר דלא ימכר דחרמים לא צריך הקדש נינהו והקדש אין הרשות ביד בעלים למוכרו לאחרים אלא לגזבר נמסר וה"נ כל כמה דאיתנהו ביד בעלים לא מזדבן חולין נינהו ונמכרין תנהו ענין למעשר דלא ימכר וכן עיקר:
notes.en: It stands to reason that we apply it to the tithe, since redemption [geula] is written with regard to it as well. So I have heard. But I have much to reply. First, that he says, “If with the owner, they are consecrated” — but consecrated property is subject to redemption, for items consecrated for Temple maintenance are redeemed like items consecrated for the altar, as it is written, “And if the one who consecrated it will redeem his house”; so you are forced to say that it was necessary to write “it shall not be redeemed” with regard to dedications. And further, that he says, “Apply it to the matter of the tithe” — why must we bring “it shall not be redeemed” to the tithe, when “it shall not be redeemed” is already stated with regard to it? And if he means it for selling, he should have said further, “If it is not relevant to redemption, apply it to selling.” Alternatively, he should have said, “Why do I need ‘it shall not be redeemed’ of dedications? Conclude from it that it is to be free, and to derive a verbal analogy: just as here selling is with it, so too with the tithe selling is with it.” Therefore it seems to me that you must read it this way: Rava says, “‘It shall not be sold’ of dedications is not needed.” And this is its explanation: Rava says that we derive without a verbal analogy that the tithe is not sold, since “it shall not be sold” of dedications is not needed. [If they are with the owner,] they are consecrated, and with consecrated property the owner has no authority to sell it to others; rather, it is handed over to the Temple treasurer. And so too here, as long as they are in the owner’s possession they are not sold; [in the priest’s possession,] they are non-sacred and are sold. Apply it to the matter of the tithe, that it shall not be sold. And this is the main [reading].

messages.text: Rashi, followed by Tosafot, questions the printed reading of Rava’s statement and proposes that it read “‘It may not be sold’ of dedications is not needed” (see Rashi’s note on the reply above, and Tosafot on Rava’s statement on 32a).

§ The prohibition against selling the animal tithe offering is not derived from dedications, but rather from the case of the animal tithe offering itself. The phrase “It may not be redeemed,” written with regard to the animal tithe offering, is to be understood as meaning: It may not be sold.
From where do I say this? As it is written: “Then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed”.

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.he: מדלא אסר ליה אלא מחיים דאי גאולה בבעלים דוקא ולמידק הא לאחר שחיטה נגאל ותופס את דמיו:
notes.en: From where do I say it: since it prohibited it only while alive; for if it were redemption by the owner specifically, one would infer that after slaughter it is redeemed and its sanctity is transferred to its money.

messages.text: When does the animal tithe offering render a non-sacred animal for which it is exchanged consecrated as a substitute? Only when the animal tithe offering is alive. Similarly, when may the animal tithe offering not be redeemed by its owner? Only when it is alive, which indicates that it may be redeemed after its slaughter.

But when redeeming a sanctified animal, it requires standing and valuation, i.e., it has to be set standing before a priest for him to evaluate it and only then is it redeemed (see Leviticus 27:11–12). How, then, can the animal tithe offering be redeemed after having been slaughtered?

notes.he: ודאי ליתיה בתורת פדיון כלל ואינו קדוש לתפוס את דמיו בקדושה והאי לא יגאל לא ימכר הוא ומשום דעביד ביה עובדא דחול קאסר ליה רחמנא הילכך מחיים דחמירא קדושתיה אסור לאחר שחיטה דאקלישא קדושתיה דהא נשחט בחוץ לאכילת זרים שרי למכור:
notes.en: It requires standing and valuation; rather: certainly it is not subject to the law of redemption at all, and it is not sacred [enough] to transfer its sanctity to its money. And this “it shall not be redeemed” is “it shall not be sold,” and it is because one performs with it an act of the non-sacred that the Merciful One prohibited it. Therefore, while alive, when its sanctity is strong, it is prohibited; after slaughter, when its sanctity has weakened, since it is slaughtered outside [the Temple] to be eaten by non-priests, it is permitted to sell.

notes.dh: הא לאחר שחיטה נגאל הא בעי העמדה והערכה
notes.he: תימה לוקמה במפרכסת דהרי היא כחיה לכל דבריה כדאמר בפ"ב דחולין (דף ל.) מדמי פסח מי אדחי הא תנא שחט בה שנים או רוב שנים כו' וי"ל דשמא זו היתה חשובה כחיה אף לענין תמורה והרב רבי שמעון מנייביל"א זצ"ל היה מפרש דהכא דנגמרה השחיטה כהלכתה לא חשיבא מפרכסת כחיה והכל פירשתי במרובה (ב"ק דף עו.) בשמעתין דפרה מטמאה טומאת אוכלין:
notes.en: But after slaughter it is redeemed; but it requires standing and valuation: It is puzzling: let him establish it as a case where it is still convulsing, for it is like a living animal in all respects, as it says in the second chapter of Chullin (30a): “Was the money of the paschal offering rejected? But it is taught: If one slaughtered in it both organs or most of both,” etc. One can say that perhaps this would be considered like a living animal also with regard to substitution. And the Rav Rabbi Shimon of Joinville, of blessed memory, would explain that here, where the slaughter was completed properly, a convulsing animal is not considered like a living one. And I explained it all in [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 76a), in the discussion of the cow that imparts the impurity of food.

notes.he: קודם שיגאל ואי אפשר להעמידן שכבר נשחט אלא ש"מ לא ימכר הוא:
notes.en: But this requires standing and valuation: before it is redeemed, and it is impossible to stand them up, since it has already been slaughtered. Rather, conclude from it that it means “it shall not be sold.”

messages.text: Rather, conclude from this verse that the phrase “it may not be redeemed” is not referring to redemption. Rather, it is actually to be understood as: It may not be sold. Accordingly, the prohibition against selling the animal tithe offering is in effect only while it is alive, as is the halakha with regard to a substitute; but once it is slaughtered, it may be sold.

This works out well according to the one who says that animals consecrated to be sacrificed on the altar that were disqualified due to a blemish were included in the requirement of standing and valuation. But according to the one who says that animals consecrated to be sacrificed on the altar that were disqualified due to a blemish were not included in the requirement of standing and valuation, what is there to say? According to this opinion, the phrase “It may not be redeemed” can be interpreted literally, in contrast to Rav Ashi’s claim.

notes.dh: הניחא למ"ד קדשי מזבח היו בכלל
notes.he: מצות העמדה והערכה אמרת דלא מתריץ בלא יגאל ממש:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says altar offerings were included: in the mitzva of standing and valuation. You said [so], since it is not resolved with “it shall not be redeemed” literally.

messages.text: This is what we said, i.e., this is what we meant. The phrase “It may not be redeemed” cannot be understood literally, as is there ever an instance where an animal may not be redeemed when alive, and yet it may be redeemed after its slaughter? Since such a scenario is impossible, the verse must be referring to the prohibition against selling.

notes.he: אמר לך רב אשי אנן הכי קא אמרינן כלומר מהא דייקינן דלא ימכר הוא דמי איכא מידי דמחיים כי אלים למיתפס פדיונו לא מיפריק ולאחר שחיטה דלא אלים מיפריק אלא ש"מ דהאי לא יגאל לא ימכר הוא:
notes.en: But according to the one who says, etc.: Rav Ashi would say to you: this is what we said. That is, from this we infer that it means “it shall not be sold”: for is there anything that, while alive, when it is strong enough to transfer its sanctity to its redemption, is not redeemed, and after slaughter, when it is not strong, is redeemed? Rather, conclude from it that this “it shall not be redeemed” is “it shall not be sold.”

messages.text: But why can it not be said that an animal may be redeemed only after its slaughter? One can claim that when the animal is alive, since its sanctity is strong, it is logical to say that it may not be redeemed. Conversely, after its slaughter, when its sanctity is weak, it is logical to claim that it may be redeemed. If so, the phrase can be understood literally.

But isn’t the opposite claim, that a slaughtered animal tithe offering may not be redeemed, based on an a fortiori inference: If, when the animal tithe offering is alive and its sanctity is strong enough to transfer that sanctity to its redemption money, just as it renders a non-sacred animal consecrated as a substitute, nevertheless it may not be redeemed, then after its slaughter, when its sanctity is not strong enough to transfer that sanctity to its redemption money, as at this stage it cannot render a non-sacred animal consecrated as a substitute, should it be able to be redeemed?
messages.quote: after its slaughter, when its sanctity is weak, it may be redeemed

messages.text: In other words, the fact that substitution can be effected only with a living animal indicates that a strong sanctity is more easily transferable to another item than a weak sanctity. Rather, conclude from this that the phrase “It may not be redeemed” is actually to be understood as meaning that it may not be sold.
But if so, let the Merciful One write explicitly: It may not be sold.

notes.he: גאולה משמע בבעלים ותופס ליה פדיונו דאי אין תופס פדיונו למה להו לבעליו לפדותו אלא לאו ש"מ לא ימכר משום עובדין דחול קאסר ליה קרא:
notes.en: Redemption implies [redemption] by the owner, with its redemption money taking on its sanctity; for if its redemption money did not take on its sanctity, why would its owner redeem it? Rather, conclude from it [that it means] “it shall not be sold”: the verse prohibited it because of acts of the non-sacred.

messages.text: Had the Merciful One written: It may not be sold, I would say that the animal tithe offering only may not be sold, as one who does so performs an act of a non-sacred item, by treating the consecrated animal in the same manner as a non-sacred animal and transferring its value to non-sacred money. But I would say that it may be redeemed, as in this manner its value becomes consecrated. Therefore, in order to counter this notion, the Merciful One writes: “It may not be redeemed,” which teaches both that the animal tithe offering may not be sold and that it may not be redeemed.
messages.quote: let the Merciful One write explicitly: It may not be sold

notes.he: דמדאפיק מכירה בלשון גאולה שמע מינה דלא איזדבוני מיזדבן הוא ולא אפרוקי מיפריק ובגאולה גרידתא ליכא לאוקמה דא"כ לא מצינן למידק הא לאחר שחיטה נגאל:
notes.en: That is why it wrote “it shall not be redeemed”: since it expressed selling in the language of redemption, conclude from it that it may not be sold and may not be redeemed. And it cannot be established as redemption alone, for if so we could not infer that after slaughter it is redeemed.

messages.text: Mishna
Beit Shammai say: An Israelite cannot be counted with the priest to partake of a blemished firstborn.

notes.he: אפי' אם זימן כהן אורח ישראל על הבכור בעל מום לא יאכל עמו:
notes.en: Mishna. He shall not be counted: even if a priest invited an Israelite guest to [partake of] the blemished firstborn, he may not eat with him.

notes.he: על הבכור בעל מום לאוכלו עמו:
notes.en: An Israelite shall not be counted with the priest: on a blemished firstborn, to eat it with him.

messages.text: And Beit Hillel deem it permitted for him to partake of it, and they deem it permitted even for a gentile to partake of a blemished firstborn.
Gemara
Whose opinion is expressed in the mishna? It is the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דשרי עובד כוכבים באכילת בכור:
notes.en: Gemara. The mishna: which permits a gentile to eat the firstborn.

notes.dh: פסק מתני' מני רבי עקיבא היא
notes.he: ואומר ר"י דהלכתא כב"ה דמתניתין דשרו אפי' לעובד כוכבים ולא כב"ה דברייתא דאסרי ופליגי אר' עקיבא דהוי סתם במתני' ומחלוקת בברייתא דהוי הלכתא כסתם דמתני' כדאיתא בהחולץ (יבמות דף מב:) וכ"ש דהכא דסתם לן כלשון ברייתא דעדיף משאר סתמי כדאיתא בסוף שבת (דף קנז.) והא דפרישנא בסמוך טעמא דרבי עקיבא מדכתיב כצבי וכאיל ואמרינן דאידך מוקים לה כר' אלעזר הקפר פי' דדריש בריש פרק שני דחולין (דף כח.) מה פסולי המוקדשים בשחיטה אף צבי ואיל בשחיטה ועוף אין לו שחיטה אלא מדברי סופרים משמע דר"ע לית ליה דרבי אלעזר הקפר אלא סבר לה כרבי דדריש שחיטה מוזבחת כאשר צויתיך מלמד שנצטוה משה על רוב אחד בעוף ועל רוב שנים בבהמה דלמא הכי קיי"ל כרבי ואע"ג דרבי יוסי בר חנינא בנזיר בפרק מי שאמר (נזיר דף כט.) סובר דאין שחיטה לעוף מה"ת אין ראיה ממנו שיהא הלכה כן דתנא הוא כדמוכח התם ועוד דר"ע מצי סבר כר' אלעזר הקפר וגמר חד מצבי וחד מאיל כדפרישית לעיל בפ' שני (בכורות דף טו.) גבי מה צבי ואיל פטורין מן הבכורה כו' ובהלכות גדולות משמע שרוצה לפסוק כב"ה דברייתא ומשמע נמי דמדרבנן היא דפליגי ארבי עקיבא דפירשו שהחלב מותר לעובד כוכבים משום דאיתקש פסולי המוקדשים לאיל וצבי והבשר אסור להאכילו לעובד כוכבים מדרבנן ואין להביא ראיה דאסור לעובד כוכבים משום דקי"ל כההוא דרשא ואכלת ולא לכלביך וה"ה לעובד כוכבים כדמוכח בפ' כל שעה (פסחים דף כט.) דאשכחן כמה סתמי כהך דאיתא הכא בפרק הלוקח בהמה (בכורות דף כא:) לעיל גבי חררת דם דתנן יקבר ובפרק עד כמה (לעיל בכורות דף כח.) מי שאינו מומחה וראה את הבכור ונשחט על פיו הרי זה יקבר ולקמן בפרקין (בכורות דף לז.) השוחט את הבכור ונודע (עד) שלא הראהו כו' הבשר יקבר ובפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין דף סט:) גבי יצא רובו ה"ז יקבר אבל היך אין ראיה דשפיר אתיא כר"ע דהא לר"ע גופיה שמעינן ליה בפרק טבול יום (זבחים דף קג: וקד.) דאמר מדבריו למדנו שהשוחט את הבכור ונמצא טריפה שיאותו הכהנים בעורו משמע דבשרם אסור בהנאה והיינו טעמא כדפרישנא לעיל בפ' שני (בכורות דף יד.) גבי קדשים שקדם מום קבוע להקדשן דהיכא דשרי לישראל הוא דאיתקש לצבי ואיל ושרי אפילו לעובד כוכבים ולא איתסר מואכלת ולא לכלביך אבל היכא דאסור לישראל לא איתקש לצבי ואיל הילכך בכור שמת או נשחט בלא התרה או הותר ונמצא טריפה טעון קבורה כדמוכח הני סתמי ואפי' רבי עקיבא מודה כדאמר בפ' טבול יום (זבחים דף קד.) ואף ר"ע לא אמר שיהא העור מותר אפי' בגבולין אלא כשהתירו מומחה אבל לא התירו מומחה לא ובטריפה נמי ואע"ג דשרי ר"ע העור אין הלכה כמותו כדמסקינן התם והלכתא כחכמים דאמרי אין לא ראיתי ראיה אלא יצא לבית השריפה ומיהו לדידן לא בעי שריפה דהתם במקדש הוא דבעי שריפה דבמקדש קאי ומ"ש שם בספרים והלכתא כחכמים בשר בקבורה והעור בשריפה פי' שם רש"י דלא גרס ליה דרבנן דאמרי בעור אלא יצא לבית השריפה לאו אדר"ע קיימי דאיירי בבכור בגבולין אלא אדרבי חנינא דאיירי בקדשי המקדש ומיהו קשיא בברייתא דלקמן בשמעתין (בכורות דף לג.) גבי שתי חטאות אחת תמימה ואחת בעלת מום דקאמר ר' אלעזר בר"ש אפי' בשר בעלת מום בקדרה ונזרק דמה של תמימה אסורה וקתני עלה בתמורה בפ' ולד חטאת (דף כד.) יוצא לבית השריפה והשתא מאיזה טעם היא בשריפה כל עיקר פסולה לא הוי אלא משום דהויא כחטאת שכפרו בעליה דמתה וחטאות המתות דינם כשמתו ואי משום דכי נשחטו הויא ליה כעין קדשים פסולים שנפסלו אחר שחיטה שיוצאים לבית השריפה הא בבכור תנן דסבר כשנשחט שלא על פי מומחה וכשנמצא טריפה הוי בקבורה כדפרישית ושמא יש לחלק בין בזמן הזה לזמן בית המקדש ואם היינו מחלקים בין נשחט שלא על פי מומחה לשאר פסול שאירע אחר שחיטה היתה מיושבת גירסת הספרים דזבחים אלא שנגרוס אפכא והלכתא כחכמים בשר בשריפה ועור בקבורה ובזמן הזה הוא דקאמר שלא החמירו על העור לשורפו כמו הבשר וא"ת מ"ש הא במס' ערלה (פ"ג מ"ג) ומייתי לה בפ"ב דתמורה (דף לד.) האורג מלא הסיט מצמר הבכור ידלק הבגד ובכל הנך שהבאתי משמע דדינו של בכור בקבורה ואין לחלק בין שער לשער דכה"ג פריך משער נזיר ופטר חמור דתנן התם יקבר ובמס' ערלה (שם) תנן בשער ובפטר חמור ידלק ואין נראה לדחות דהתם פריך משום דמשמע ליה מתני' התם דקתני שער נזיר ופטר חמור דקאי שער אתרוייהו ועוד תניא נמי בתוספתא התולש צמר מבכור תם והניחו בחלון אע"ג שנולד לו מום לאחר מכאן ושחטו הרי זה יקבר וי"ל דאיכא לשנויי הכא כדמשני התם אפטר חמור כאן בשק כאן בשער פי' שער ממהר לכלות וסגי ליה בקבורה אבל אם עשה ממנו בגד חיישינן שמא יוציאוהו אחר שנקבר ובעי שריפה ואיכא דמשני התם ומוקי לה כר' יהודה דאמר אם רצה להחמיר על עצמו לשרוף את הנקברים רשאי:
notes.en: In brief: Ruling. The Ri says the halakha follows Beit Hillel of the mishna, who permit even a gentile, and not Beit Hillel of the baraita, who prohibit and disagree with Rabbi Akiva: where there is an unattributed mishna and a dispute in a baraita, the halakha follows the unattributed mishna (Yevamot 42b), all the more so here, where the mishna is unattributed in the very wording of the baraita, which is stronger than other unattributed rulings (Shabbat 157a). Tosafot then discusses the reason given below for Rabbi Akiva, “as the gazelle and as the deer,” and Rabbi Elazar HaKappar’s derivation (Chullin 28a): this implies that Rabbi Akiva holds like Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], that birds require slaughter by Torah law, and Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina (Nazir 29a) is no proof otherwise; alternatively, Rabbi Akiva may hold like Rabbi Elazar HaKappar and derive one point from the gazelle and one from the deer (see 15a). Halakhot Gedolot seems to rule like Beit Hillel of the baraita, the meat being prohibited to a gentile only by rabbinic law, while the fat is permitted since disqualified consecrated animals are compared to the gazelle and deer. There is no proof of a prohibition for gentiles from “you may eat, and not your dogs” (Pesachim 29a), nor from the unattributed rulings that a blemished firstborn must be buried (21b, 28a, 37a; Chullin 69b): those concern a firstborn prohibited to an Israelite as well, which is not compared to the gazelle and deer, as even Rabbi Akiva agrees (Zevachim 103b–104a; see 14a). Tosafot discusses at length whether such meat and hide are buried or burned (the reading in Zevachim, Rashi there, the baraita of two sin offerings below on 33a with Temura 24a), suggesting distinctions between Temple times and nowadays; and asks from Orla 3:3 (Temura 34a), where a garment woven of firstborn wool is burned, answering that hair decays and burial suffices, while a garment might be dug up and used, or that the mishna there follows Rabbi Yehuda, who allows one to be stringent and burn what is to be buried. It also cites a Tosefta about wool plucked from an unblemished firstborn. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: In the case of a blemished firstborn offering, only a group constituted entirely of priests may be counted to partake of it; this is the statement of Beit Shammai. And Beit Hillel say: The group may even be constituted of non-priests.
Beit Hillel deem it permitted even for a gentile to partake of a blemished firstborn.

notes.he: דמתיר אליבא דב"ה קאמר ר' עקיבא דבית הלל מתירין אפי' עובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Whose is it? It is Rabbi Akiva’s: who permits [it], and he says it according to Beit Hillel: Rabbi Akiva says that Beit Hillel permit even a gentile.

messages.text: Evidently, Beit Hillel’s opinion in the mishna is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva’s explanation in this baraita.

What is the reason of Beit Shammai? As it is written in a verse discussing the firstborn offering, addressed to Aaron and his sons: “But the firstling of an ox, or the firstling of a sheep, or the firstling of a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy …and their flesh shall be yours, as the wave breast and as the right thigh, it shall be yours” (Numbers 18:17–18).
messages.quote: An Israelite cannot be counted with the priest

verse.he: וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: But their meat shall be yours: it shall be yours like the breast of elevation offering and like the right thigh.

messages.text: Just as there, with regard to the breast and the thigh, priests may partake of it but an Israelite, i.e., a non-priest, may not, as the verse states: “You shall eat in a pure place; you, and your sons, and your daughters with you” (Leviticus 10:14), so too here, with regard to the firstborn offering, only priests may partake of it, but an Israelite may not.

verse.he: וְאֵת חֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וְאֵת ׀ שׁוֹק הַתְּרוּמָה תֹּאכְלוּ בְּמָקוֹם טָהוֹר אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ וּבְנֹתֶיךָ אִתָּךְ כִּי־חׇקְךָ וְחׇק־בָּנֶיךָ נִתְּנוּ מִזִּבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en: But the breast of elevation offering and the thigh of gift offering you [and your wife], and your sons and daughters with you, may eat in any pure place, for they have been assigned as a due to you and your sons from the Israelites’ sacrifices of well-being.

notes.dh: מה בחזה ושוק כהנים אין ישראל לא
notes.he: דכתיב ואתה ובניך ובנותיך אתך:
notes.en: Just as with the breast and thigh, priests yes, Israelites no: as it is written, “You, and your sons, and your daughters with you.”

messages.text: Continued on 33a: Beit Hillel answer that this applies to an unblemished firstborn, while of a blemished one it is written “the impure and the pure may eat it alike.”
